title: MTRX™ Field Series No. 07 · Design and taste · Kevin Cecil

cards.name: Why do a safari website and a Kubrick frame need the same eye?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "Why do a safari website and a Kubrick frame need the same eye?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Train the eye first. Every craft after it gets cheaper to learn.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: What is design, if it is not decoration?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "What is design, if it is not decoration?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Design is a plan with a purpose. Decoration is what you get when the purpose goes missing.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: What problem are we actually designing?
cards.q: What did the 1972 subway map get wrong, according to the riders?
options: It did not help them relate the subway to the streets above
Its colours were too dull to tell the routes apart on the platform
It was drawn too small to read the station names anywhere
cards.why: The diagram made routes legible but drew geography loosely, so riders could not place themselves above ground.

cards.name: What problem are we actually designing?
cards.q: Which line is a usable problem frame for a safari website?
options: Make the homepage feel more premium than every competitor in the region
Use bigger wildlife photos and a darker, more elegant palette
How might a first-time guest compare lodges and keep the wonder?
cards.why: A frame names a person, a task and a feeling. The others are requests for a look.

cards.name: What problem are we actually designing?
cards.q: How did Eames describe design constraints?
options: As obstacles a talented designer should negotiate away early
As limits that often imply an ethic, to work within with enthusiasm
As details for the engineers, kept well away from the creative idea itself
cards.why: Eames: there are always design constraints, and these often imply an ethic.

cards.name: What problem are we actually designing?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "What problem are we actually designing?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Beautiful work on the wrong problem is still the wrong work.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: How do designers get from fog to a decision?
cards.q: What does the first diamond of the Double Diamond produce?
options: A moodboard of attractive references in the client's style
A clearly defined problem, found by going wide first
A finished prototype, ready for the client to approve
cards.why: Discover and Define find the right problem. Develop and Deliver find the right solution.

cards.name: How do designers get from fog to a decision?
cards.q: What did the Eameses say you must do first, before designing a lota?
options: Shut out preconceived ideas and consider factor after factor
Study the most beautiful antique lotas and copy their proportions
Ask the government which modern material the factories preferred
cards.why: The report lists the factors: liquid, hands, transport, balance, pouring, filling and cleaning.

cards.name: How do designers get from fog to a decision?
cards.q: What was Natasha Jen's main complaint about design thinking?
options: Designers should never talk to the people who will use their work
Research slows projects down and should be left to market analysts
Its marketing sells a tidy diagram as if it gave you design judgement
cards.why: She objects to the workshop version, not to thinking like a designer. Craft and responsibility still matter.

cards.name: How do designers get from fog to a decision?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "How do designers get from fog to a decision?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Go wide before you decide, then kill ideas for reasons you can say out loud.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: What does the eye grab first, and what does it miss?
cards.q: Why is an orange circle among orange squares and grey circles slow to find?
options: Circles are always noticed more slowly than squares
It shares one feature with each kind of neighbour
Orange is harder for the eye to see than grey is
cards.why: A conjunction of features needs focused search. A single unique feature pops out.

cards.name: What does the eye grab first, and what does it miss?
cards.q: What did Yarbus show with the Repin painting?
options: The scan path through a picture changes with the viewer's task
All viewers follow the same fixed path through any picture they see
People look mostly at the brightest part of any painting
cards.why: The scan paths changed with each question. The original was one observer; replications found a smaller effect.

cards.name: What does the eye grab first, and what does it miss?
cards.q: What does the NN/g 2017 update say about the F-pattern?
options: It is a fixed law of reading that every web page should be built around
It was disproved, so text layout has no effect on scanning
It is common on dense text, and good layout can prevent it
cards.why: The F is a warning about walls of text, not an instruction to put everything top left.

cards.name: What does the eye grab first, and what does it miss?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "What does the eye grab first, and what does it miss?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Attention is a spotlight steered by the task. Design for what people are trying to do, not for how you hope they will look.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: What are point, line, plane, shape and form doing?
cards.q: What were Kandinsky's three basic elements in his 1926 Bauhaus book?
options: Point, line and the basic plane
Hue, value and the colour wheel
Colour, texture and the pattern grid
cards.why: Point and Line to Plane has chapters on the point, the line and the basic plane.

cards.name: What are point, line, plane, shape and form doing?
cards.q: What did the 2021 study of bouba and kiki in 25 languages find?
options: The effect appears only for speakers who grew up reading the Roman alphabet
Strong evidence that the match holds across languages and scripts
People pair the words with shapes at random once tested fairly
cards.why: Roman-script readers were only marginally more likely to show it. The effect did not depend on the shape of letters.

cards.name: What are point, line, plane, shape and form doing?
cards.q: How should a designer treat shape language, such as triangles meaning danger?
options: As a strong rule of thumb, to test on real viewers
As a proven law of perception that works the same everywhere
As a myth with no connection to how people perceive shapes
cards.why: It rides on real shape and sound correspondences, but context and culture still change the reading.

cards.name: What are point, line, plane, shape and form doing?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "What are point, line, plane, shape and form doing?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Feeling starts below the content: in the marks, their direction and their weight.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: Why do designers squint?
cards.q: Why does a squint test help a designer?
options: It shows exactly where a typical visitor will look first and last
It proves that a design meets the web accessibility standard
It blurs detail and colour, leaving the masses of light and dark
cards.why: It is a rule of thumb for value and hierarchy, not a measure of real gaze or accessibility.

cards.name: Why do designers squint?
cards.q: MTRX orange on white scores about 3.16 to 1. Where can you use it?
options: Nowhere on a website, because it fails every test
Anywhere, because orange is a strong and vivid hue
Large headings and buttons, but not body text
cards.why: Body text needs 4.5 to 1. Large text and interface parts need 3 to 1.

cards.name: Why do designers squint?
cards.q: What did Dow mean by notan?
options: The order in which colours should be applied
The pattern of dark and light masses in a design
A Japanese ideal of perfect simplicity, emptiness and calm
cards.why: Notan is the arrangement of dark and light, studied in two or three values before colour.

cards.name: Why do designers squint?
cards.q: Page closed: explain "Why do designers squint?" in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Value first. If it works in grey, colour can only make it better.
cards.label: Say it in the room

cards.name: More than minimal. More than bold.
cards.q: Page closed: explain "More than minimal. More than bold." in two or three lines, as you would to a client.
cards.answer: Style is a system of choices, not a bag of decorative effects.
cards.label: Say it in the room
